entries.keywords: continents seven continents africa asia europe australia antarctica america
entries.a: The world has seven continents: Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia (Oceania) and Antarctica. Africa is the second largest. There are five oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.

entries.keywords: africa countries how many countries africa 54 continent biggest
entries.a: Africa has 54 countries. The largest by area is Algeria and the most populous is Nigeria. Africa has deserts (the Sahara), rainforests (the Congo basin), grasslands (savannah) and the world's longest river, the Nile.

entries.keywords: sadc southern africa community regional countries
entries.a: SADC is the Southern African Development Community, a group of countries in southern Africa that work together on trade, peace and development. Zimbabwe is a member.

entries.keywords: african union au organisation unity
entries.a: The African Union (AU) is the organisation of African countries, founded in 2002 and based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It works on peace, trade and cooperation.

entries.keywords: united nations un organisation world peace
entries.a: The United Nations (UN) was formed in 1945 to keep peace and help countries cooperate. It has offices like UNICEF (children), WHO (health) and UNESCO (education and culture).

entries.keywords: longest river nile amazon rivers world
entries.a: The Nile in Africa is usually named as the longest river, about 6,650 km. The Amazon in South America carries the most water. Zimbabwe's great river is the Zambezi.

entries.keywords: highest mountain everest kilimanjaro tallest
entries.a: The tallest mountain on Earth is Mount Everest (about 8,849 m) in Asia. Africa's highest is Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania. Zimbabwe's highest is Mount Nyangani.

entries.keywords: sahara desert biggest hot desert
entries.a: The Sahara in northern Africa is the largest hot desert in the world. The Kalahari, which stretches across Botswana, Namibia and South Africa, is a drier savannah region in southern Africa.

entries.keywords: population world people how many billion earth
entries.a: More than 8 billion people live on Earth. The numbers change every year, so check a recent source for the exact figure.

entries.keywords: languages world most spoken english mandarin spanish swahili
entries.a: Some of the most widely spoken languages are English, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi, Spanish and Arabic. In Africa, Swahili, Hausa and Arabic have very many speakers. Zimbabwe has 16 official languages.

entries.keywords: time zones time difference gmt world clock
entries.a: The world is divided into time zones because the Earth turns and the sun rises at different times. Zimbabwe uses Central Africa Time, which is GMT+2, all year with no daylight saving.

entries.keywords: capital cities africa zambia mozambique south africa botswana namibia kenya nigeria ghana
entries.a: Some capitals: Zambia - Lusaka; Mozambique - Maputo; South Africa - Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), Bloemfontein (judicial); Botswana - Gaborone; Namibia - Windhoek; Malawi - Lilongwe; Tanzania - Dodoma; Kenya - Nairobi; Nigeria - Abuja; Ghana - Accra; Egypt - Cairo.

entries.keywords: climate change global warming greenhouse gases carbon emissions
entries.a: Burning coal, oil and gas and cutting down forests add greenhouse gases that warm the planet. Effects include droughts, floods and stronger storms. We can help by planting trees, saving energy, using solar and wasting less.

entries.keywords: why seasons earth tilt orbit sun day night rotation
entries.a: Day and night happen because the Earth rotates once every 24 hours. Seasons happen because the Earth's axis is tilted as it orbits the sun, once every year (365 days). In the southern hemisphere, summer is around December.

entries.keywords: moon phases lunar full moon new moon orbit month
entries.a: The Moon orbits the Earth about every 27 days and shines by reflecting sunlight. Its shape seems to change because we see more or less of its lit side: new moon, crescent, quarter, full moon.

entries.keywords: planets solar system order mercury venus earth mars jupiter saturn uranus neptune
entries.a: The eight planets in order from the sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. A memory trick: 'My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Naming'. Jupiter is the biggest.

entries.keywords: wonders world great wall pyramids taj mahal famous landmarks
entries.a: Famous landmarks include the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, the Great Wall of China, the Taj Mahal in India, Machu Picchu in Peru, and Victoria Falls on the Zimbabwe-Zambia border.

entries.keywords: world war history first second world war 1914 1939
entries.a: World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918 and World War II from 1939 to 1945. Millions of people died. The UN was created afterwards to help prevent such wars.

entries.keywords: africa independence decolonisation ghana 1957 kenya 1963 zambia 1964 south africa 1994
entries.a: Many African countries gained independence between the 1950s and 1970s: Ghana in 1957, Kenya in 1963, Zambia in 1964, Mozambique in 1975, Zimbabwe in 1980, Namibia in 1990. South Africa held its first democratic election in 1994.

entries.keywords: currency money exchange rate dollar euro pound rand zig
entries.a: Each country has a currency, such as the US dollar, euro, pound, South African rand and Botswana pula. Zimbabwe uses US dollars and its own currency, the ZiG. An exchange rate shows how much one currency is worth in another and it changes.
